notes: Summary: POC completed (search / rerank) — model perf OK; decision went to hyperscaler managed endpoints.
Timeline: engaged Sep 2025, POC kickoff Nov 2025, demo + perf review Jan 2026, procurement decision Feb 2026.
Why lost: finance + infra preference for single-cloud managed service (SageMaker) — citing faster path to production and simplified billing.
Quote from Head of ML (call 2026-02-10): "We want the operational surface to be AWS-native — it's a hard mandate from Infra."
Security: initially concerned about data residency and audit logs; Redwood satisfied most items in security FAQ but infra still required in-house managed endpoint with existing IAM/KMS ties.
Cost: Redwood TCO looked competitive on token-unit basis but infra team flagged integration work and one-off migration costs vs. AWS managed offering (migration discount offered by AWS).
Champion: product lead (Maya) got promoted in Dec; no replacement owner — lost momentum internally.
Action items before close: provided deployment runbook, security attestation, and cost comparison deck (see drive link). No counter-offer submitted after procurement final decision.
Follow-up plan: re-engage in Q4 2026 after liftgate re-evaluates multi-cloud strategy; monitor AWS usage signals (if available) for vulnerability window.

Internal AE notes: very responsive early, then slow after promotion; procurement said
"if it adds another vendor we need exec sign-off" — they didn’t get it.
POC artifacts: sample embeddings + reranker tests — outcome: 15% CTR lift in product search, latency 60-120ms at 95th pctl for test shard (hosted config).
Escalations: raised integration complexity to PLAT-5121 (Jira) — infra wanted native VPC endpoints managed by AWS.
Suggested touchpoints: security refresh, cost repricing, and case studies of customers who later migrated off hyperscaler managed endpoints.
Potential upside: if LiftGate decides to run private instances for data residency or multi-cloud failover, revisit contract discussions.
